ai_disclosure: AI was used to read the regulation text into rule candidates. Values labeled 'Derived' come from readings that passed review; values labeled 'Interpretation' come from readings not yet reviewed, or depend on a condition the engine does not model. In this demo the review was first an AI review applied on the project owner's instruction; the project owner then approved most of the rules the engine reads, in bulk from a review sheet, and the rest rest on the AI review alone. Each value's source panel says which. No AI model is used to compute this assessment.
disclaimers: Decision support for licensed professionals, not a zoning determination. Confirm every result with the jurisdiction before relying on it: LA City Planning and LADBS in the City, LA County Regional Planning and Public Works in unincorporated areas.
Parcel boundaries and attributes come from the Los Angeles County Assessor's open parcel data, provided for informational purposes; it may not be suitable for legal, engineering, or surveying use.

items.explanation: Lot is 60 ft wide (50 ft or more): 5 ft for a building up to two stories and 18 ft. New construction adds 1 ft for each 10 ft (or part) of height above 18 ft (LAMC 12.08 C.2(b)), so this shows 7 ft for a 33 ft house (the maximum). By height: 5 ft up to 18 ft, 6 ft up to 28 ft, 7 ft up to 33 ft. Walls over 14 ft high and 45 ft long need a 5 ft deep, 10 ft long plane break (enter a wall length under Your project to check it).

items.explanation: 0.45 x lot area (8,100 sq ft), for a lot outside the Hillside Area and Coastal Zone. The encroachment plane that starts 20 ft above the front and side yards is not drawn. What counts (LAMC 12.03): area under a ceiling over 14 ft counts twice; required covered parking is not counted up to 400 sq ft when all of it is in the rear half or at least 55 ft from the front (otherwise 200 sq ft), nor detached accessory buildings of 200 sq ft or less, up to 400 sq ft in all. Lattice-roof porches and qualifying basements are not counted either.

items.explanation: The lot is within half a mile, in a straight line, of a major transit stop or high-quality transit corridor in Caltrans' layer (a frequent bus corridor). State law allows 18 ft within half a mile walking distance, plus 2 ft for a roof pitch that matches the house, so up to 20 ft. Walking distance can be longer than the straight line; confirm it, or plan for 16 ft.

items.explanation: Up to 2 homes on the lot, approved ministerially (Gov. Code 65852.21(a)). Local standards may not prevent two units of at least 800 sq ft each, and side and rear setbacks may be at most 4 ft (none for an existing structure rebuilt in place) (65852.21(b)). Checked: the lot is in a single-family zone (R1); no historic preservation overlay (HPOZ) is mapped here. The loaded maps show no Very High fire hazard zone, earthquake fault zone or 100-year flood plain here (Gov. Code 65913.4(a)(6)(D), (F) and (G)). Still to confirm: no demolition or alteration of rent-restricted or rent-controlled housing, or housing a tenant occupied in the last 3 years; no units withdrawn from rent under the Ellis Act in the last 15 years; the Gov. Code 65913.4(a)(6) sites not mapped here: farmland (B), wetlands (C), listed hazardous waste sites (E), a regulatory floodway (H), natural community conservation plan lands (I), protected species habitat (J) and conservation easements (K). SB 9 uses that section as it read on 2021-09-16; the copy loaded here is the 2026 text, whose (B)-(K) list the same kinds of site; that the lot is not an individually listed historic resource or a City or County landmark.

items.explanation: Two new lots of about equal size, neither under 40% of the lot (3,240 sq ft) nor under 1,200 sq ft (Gov. Code 66411.7(a)). This 8,100 sq ft lot can be split into two lots of at least 3,240 sq ft (an equal split gives 4,050 sq ft each). Each new lot can then have up to two homes; the City need not allow more (66411.7(j)). The owner must sign an affidavit to live in one unit for 3 years, and a lot created by an earlier SB 9 split cannot be split again (66411.7). The loaded maps show no Very High fire hazard zone, earthquake fault zone or 100-year flood plain here (Gov. Code 65913.4(a)(6)(D), (F) and (G)).
